title: Strengths, small wins, a steady body and a circle that lifts you

say: Strengths, small wins, a steady body, and a circle that lifts you.
This is the video for module two of Confidence Building and Self-Belief.
Ask women what they are good at and many say, nothing special. Ask what neighbours come to them for, and the answers flow.
Skills are things you can do, learned through practice.

cards.d: Things you can do, learned through practice: sewing, baking, bookkeeping, braiding.
Things you know: local market prices, first aid, a language, community rules.
How you behave: kindness, honesty, perseverance, fairness, humour.

say: Character strengths are how you behave: kindness, honesty, perseverance.

For example, Kemi sells adire from home and believed she had no real skills. Then she wrote the evidence. Her savings group of 12 women has run for three years with no missing money. Twelve women trust her with their savings.

say: Doing things yourself and succeeding is the strongest source of confidence. Small wins create that on purpose.

For example, Blessing bakes cakes in Port Harcourt but is nervous about promoting herself. Her SMART goal: three new orders from people outside her family, through WhatsApp, by 30 November. Specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.

panel.heading: Blessing's four-week ladder
items: Week 1: post one cake photo, three times
Week 2: send a price list to 10 contacts
Week 3: share two customer reviews
Week 4: post in one buy-and-sell group

say: Week one is tiny: post one cake photo on her status, three times. Her confidence rating for it is 9.

say: Each week is a little bigger. Rate every step from 0 to 10. Below 7? Make it smaller.

say: She also makes an if-then plan. When I put the kids to bed on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, I will post my status.
By week 4 she has four new orders, and her confidence in self-promotion moves from 3 to 7.

say: A racing heart before a challenge is your body preparing for action. You do not have to remove that energy. You can label it differently.
For example, Zainab runs a grinding business in Kano and has a loan meeting at a microfinance bank.

items: Feet flat, shoulders relaxed
Breathe in through your nose for 4
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 6
Practise daily for at least 5 minutes
Soften your shoulders and jaw

say: She breathes in through her nose for 4, and out slowly through her mouth for 6, like blowing on hot food. She does 8 slow breaths. For daily practice, keep going for at least 5 minutes.

say: A shrinking posture squeezes your breath and your voice.

panel.heading: Shrinking or steady?
left: Eyes on the floor or phone
right: Calm pace, heard at the back
Sitting where you can be seen

say: An upright, open posture lets you breathe, project your voice and look engaged. Steady presence does not mean staring. Where culture expects it, glance down respectfully, and keep your head up and voice clear.
Wear clean clothes that fit and suit the occasion. A slipping gele or pinching shoes steal your attention.

say: After time with someone, do you usually feel more capable, or less?

panel.heading: Map who lifts you and who drains you
items: Close and lifting: share goals and wins
Distant and lifting: move them closer
Close and draining: share less, set limits
Distant and draining: mute or leave

say: Share your goals with close people who lift you. Move helpful mentors and role models closer. The best role model is a woman a step or two ahead of you, in your own town.

panel.heading: Map who lifts you and who drains you
items: Close and lifting: share goals and wins
Distant and lifting: move them closer
Close and draining: share less, set limits
Distant and draining: mute or leave

say: With close people who drain you, share less and set a boundary. For example, Esther's cousin mocks her computer class. She says calmly, I know you care about me. I have decided to do this course. Let us talk about something else.
And mute or leave groups that make you feel small.

say: To remember. Back your strengths with evidence. Take small steps you can finish. Breathe slowly and stand tall. And build a circle that lifts you.
If someone at home controls you through threats, fear or violence, that is more than a confidence issue. Your safety comes first. Speak to someone you trust, and in an emergency call 112.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Back every strength with real evidence
Small SMART steps you rate 7 or more
Breathe in for 4, out for 6
Upright posture, clothes that fit
Spend time with people who lift you
